title: Private House Design 160 m², Munich | DUMSKAYA DESIGN
description: 160 m² private house in Munich: interior design, 3D visualization, technical drawings, custom furniture and turnkey renovation.
h1: Private house interior design project, Munich, Germany, 160 m²

blocks.text: Private house interior design project, Munich, Germany, 160 m²

parts.html: A 160 m² private house in Munich. Here we covered the whole cycle: interior design project with 3D visualization, technical documentation, custom furniture and turnkey renovation. Before the renovation started, the client received a detailed cost estimate for the work, materials, furniture, appliances, plumbing fixtures and lighting.

The furniture for the living room, kitchen, bedroom, walk-in closets, entrance hall and bathrooms was designed for this house. We make it at our own workshop in Bratislava and deliver it with installation, including to Germany. The gallery starts with the visualizations, followed by photos of the finished house.

blocks.text: Living room, dining area and kitchen

parts.html: The living room, dining area and kitchen form a single space with floor-to-ceiling windows onto the terrace. The wall behind the sofa was finished in light gray vertical slats; in the finished house it holds round moss panels in brass frames. Opposite the sofa is a plain wall with concealed doors and a low wall-hung TV unit, and next to it a built-in light wood shelving unit with lit shelves.

A cluster of clear glass globes hangs above the dining table with its glass top, and the chairs are upholstered in gray-brown velvet. Lighting comes from ceiling tracks with linear fixtures. The windows have sheer curtains and heavy taupe drapes.

The kitchen is a single run with an island: the lower fronts are white gloss and handleless, and the tall oven units are in light wood up to the ceiling. The window wall and the floor were clad in large white marble-look tiles. A wooden bar counter is attached to the island.

In the bedroom, panels cover the whole wall behind the bed: smooth concrete-look panels in the center, herringbone veneer on the sides, and a dark band with sconces at headboard height. Opposite is a wardrobe with white gloss fronts. The children’s room has sage green accents: a bed under a house-shaped canopy with string lights, a climbing wall and cube shelving for toys.

The main bathroom is tiled in light stone-look tiles, with one wall laid in a herringbone pattern. It has a freestanding bathtub, a console with two sinks and two lit mirrors. The second bathroom has a vanity with fluted wood fronts, a wall-to-wall mirrored cabinet with lit shelves and a wall in dark marble-look tiles.
